paper_metadata.title: SAPO: Improving the Scalability and Accuracy of Quantum Linear Solver for Portfolio Optimization

summary: SAPO is an HHL-based gate-model portfolio optimization method that reduces the reported HHL complexity by 34.64%-36.94% versus basic HHL on 2- to 6-asset instances, while improving accuracy by 1.52×/1.46× versus Qiskit/hybrid HHL at fixed qubit count and 1.28×/1.39× at fixed asset count. The paper also reports a 98.59% reduction in condition number and uses offline SVR-based min/max eigenvalue prediction, but it does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical portfolio optimization.

experiments.description: SAPO: HHL-based portfolio optimization with constraint scaling and min-max eigenvalue prediction, evaluated on real market datasets (Nasdaq, NYSE, AMEX) for 2- to 6-asset problems and compared against basic HHL, Qiskit HHL, and hybrid HHL.

algorithm.variant: SAPO (scaled HHL for Black's model with min-max eigenvalue predictor)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio optimization is converted from Black's model into a linear system via Lagrange multipliers; the HHL circuit solves the linear system. QPE register size depends on the condition number and target error.
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize w^T Σ w subject to w^T R = E and w^T 1 = 1 (Black's model / mean-variance portfolio optimization)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Equivalent transformation by scaling the equality constraints with factors s1 and s2; HHL normalization uses Const = |λ|min; QPE parameterization uses predicted min/max eigenvalues.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Lagrange matrix ML from Black's model, standardized as M_L^std = (l/|λ|max) M_L with l=0.5

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on market data with randomly selected stocks from Nasdaq, NYSE, and AMEX; problems range from 2 to 6 assets.

ticker_symbols: randomly selected stocks from each exchange; examples shown include SIRI, KHC, ILMN, SNPS, VRSK, ADI, REGN, MRNA, HON, ODFL, CEG
dataset_specification.preprocessing: construct return table from adjacent-day increments; compute expected return vector and covariance matrix; pad Lagrange matrix to power of 2 with zeros and identity matrix; standardize by |λ|max

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical prices are converted to returns using adjacent-day increments; expected returns and covariance matrices are computed from the past 251 days; the Lagrange matrix is padded to a power of two and standardized; eigenvalue labels are computed exactly with NumPy for predictor training.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison against basic HHL, Qiskit HHL, and hybrid HHL; complexity evaluated for absolute errors ϵ in {1/4, 1/8, 1/16}; accuracy evaluated under fixed QPE qubit counts and fixed asset counts; ablation study for scaling factor and eigenvalue predictor; 1500 cases used for eigenvalue predictor evaluation.

implementation_details.classical_solver: NumPy for exact eigenvalues; SciPy Nelder-Mead-inspired search; scikit-learn SVR for eigenvalue prediction
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: construct returns, compute covariance/expected returns, pad matrices, train SVR predictor offline, search static scaling factors offline
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: measure/obtain quantum state vector and post-process to recover portfolio weights; cosine similarity used for accuracy

speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as end-to-end complexity metric Θ, not wall-clock runtime.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log n · κ^2 / ϵ) for HHL

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; experiments cover only 2-6 assets and are simulation-based.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: HHL-style circuit with QPE, uniformly controlled RY, and inverse QPE; reported logical qubits around 11.8-13.9 and circuit depths around 4.2×10^4 to 3.7×10^5 at ϵ=1/8.
limiting_factors: Only simulation/Qiskit-based evaluation; no QPU results
No end-to-end runtime advantage over classical portfolio solvers is shown
HHL has quadratic dependence on condition number, making constant factors unfavorable
Classical preprocessing includes SVR prediction and iterative scaling search

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states implementation in Qiskit and reports circuit metrics, but no real QPU/device is named.
Speedup order set to none_proven because the paper reports asymptotic HHL complexity but does not provide a classical asymptotic baseline or proven end-to-end quantum advantage.
Nq, Nd, and N_CNOT are reported in Table IV for multiple asset counts and error settings; exact per-row values are summarized in the paper rather than a single fixed circuit size.
The paper compares against Qiskit HHL and hybrid HHL, but those are baselines within the same HHL family, not separate experiments.
The paper reports improved complexity and accuracy relative to other HHL variants, but does not compare against a strong classical portfolio optimizer end-to-end.
The claimed gains are within the HHL family and on small simulated instances, so practical quantum advantage is not demonstrated.
